title: QuoteVerify: Inference-Time Quote-Backed Citation Verification for Deep Research Reports

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is to detect and correct hallucinated or unsupported citations in long-form research reports without retraining the generator. Paper [1] explicitly addresses citation hallucinations in AI-generated content, focusing on automated verification mechanisms for bibliographic integrity. Paper [9] introduces SemanticCite, which verifies citation accuracy through full-text analysis and evidence-based reasoning, targeting semantic citation errors and AI-generated hallucinated references. Paper [14] discusses the systemic threat posed by LLM-generated "ghost citations" and develops a framework for large-scale citation verification. These papers share the same problem-class objective of addressing citation hallucinations and ensuring bibliographic integrity.

### Mechanism
The contribution uses a five-stage modular inference-time pipeline (structured citation triple generation, source fetching, quote validity checking via substring matching, NLI entailment gating, repair-or-drop). Paper [10] describes a pipeline for fact extraction and verification that includes document selection, sentence retrieval, and recognizing textual entailment (RTE), which aligns with the NLI entailment gating and evidence verification components of the contribution. Paper [12] outlines a three-step pipeline for fact verification, including document retrieval, sentence retrieval, and claim verification, which overlaps with the structured citation triple generation and evidence validation steps. Paper [23] also presents a pipeline for fact extraction and verification, incorporating document retrieval, sentence selection, and textual entailment, which matches the modular pipeline structure and NLI entailment gating. Paper [19] proposes a hybrid pipeline integrating multiple verification techniques, including evidence retrieval and entailment reasoning, which aligns with the modular pipeline approach.

### Evaluation
The contribution evaluates its method on ReportBench, demonstrating statistically significant citation-quality gains over standard baselines. Paper [9] evaluates SemanticCite using full-text analysis and evidence-based reasoning, which aligns with the evaluation design of validating citation accuracy improvements. Paper [14] conducts a large-scale study of citation validity using a framework for citation verification, which matches the evaluation design of benchmarking citation quality improvements. Paper [22] introduces a zero-assumption protocol for systematic reference verification, which involves validating citations against multiple academic databases, aligning with the evaluation design of citation-quality benchmarking. These papers share the same evaluation design of benchmarking citation verification systems, even if the specific dataset or benchmark instance differs.

### Domain
The contribution operates in the domain of citation verification for deep research agents. Paper [1] addresses citation hallucinations in AI-generated academic content, which falls within the same general application area of citation verification. Paper [9] targets citation accuracy in academic literature, addressing semantic citation errors and AI-generated hallucinated references, which aligns with the domain. Paper [14] focuses on citation validity in the context of LLM-generated academic writing, which is also part of the citation verification domain. Paper [22] develops a protocol for systematic reference verification in academic research, which is directly within the same domain.
